title: Reading narrative: Ruth 1

objectives.can: Read Ruth 1 through, following the wayyiqtol chain and the speeches, with help only where asked.

explanation.summary: Ruth 1 is a short chapter in which a family leaves home, loses its men, and sets out again. It uses the wayyiqtol chain, background clauses, dialogue, כִּי and אֲשֶׁר, which are the tools of this stage. This lesson gives you a way to read it from the first verse to the last.

sections.heading: How the chapter is built
body: The chapter falls into five parts. Each has its own mix of narrative and speech. Read it once for the shape before reading it for the grammar.
The first reading of this lesson is verses 1–15. A second reading, verses 16–22, takes the story to Ruth's vow and the arrival at Bethlehem. Verse 16 is also worked through below, word by word.

sections.heading: A way to read each verse
body: First look for the verbs. A clause that opens with a wayyiqtol is the next event. A clause that opens with something else is probably background: a description, a reason, a contrast.

Next, look for speech. A form of וַיֹּאמֶר or וַתֹּאמֶר opens it, and the first return to a wayyiqtol with a new action closes it. Inside the speech expect commands, wishes, plans and statements about the present.

Then look at the small words. כִּי is a reason, 'that', 'when' or 'but'; אֲשֶׁר opens a relative clause whose antecedent you must find. A suffix on a noun or a preposition names a person: בָנָיו, 'his sons', and אִשְׁתּוֹ, 'his wife'. A construct chain such as בִּשְׂדֵי מוֹאָב, 'in the fields of Moab', runs one noun into the next.

Last, check the gender and number of the verbs. In this chapter the women are the main speakers and actors, and the verbs often end in the feminine plural -נָה, as in וַתֵּלַכְנָה and וַתֹּאמַרְנָה. These endings tell you that two or three women act together.

sections.heading: Reading with help
body: You will not always know every word. When you meet one, do not stop. Try first to place it by its function in the clause: verb, subject, object, or a phrase with a preposition. If you can say that, you have read the sentence even before you know the meaning of the word. Then look the word up, and use what the analysed text says about its form.
The questions that follow ask about forms (stem, conjugation, person, gender, number) and about what the verses say. Both are part of reading.

misunderstandings: Reading is not translating word by word. You read a clause at a time, and look first at the verb and its place in the chain.
A feminine plural verb with -נָה does not mean a single woman. It means two or more.
A string of 'and' clauses is not a list of events of equal importance. The wayyiqtols give the main line; the other clauses support it.
The English beside the text is a help and an interpretation. It does not show which Hebrew form stands behind each word.

deeper.heading: Why the feminine plural matters in Ruth
body: Hebrew has a special feminine plural in the yiqtol and wayyiqtol, with the ending -נָה. It is much less common than the masculine plural, because most subjects in the Bible are men or mixed groups, but it is frequent in Ruth 1 because the three women are the actors. In Ruth 1:19 the plural וַתֵּלַכְנָה, 'and the two of them went', is followed by the feminine singular וַתֵּהֹם, 'was stirred', for the whole town.

quoted.title: Ruth
quoted.english: AND IT came to pass in the days when the judges judged, that there was a famine in the land. And a certain man of Beth-lehem in Judah went to sojourn in the field of Moab, he, and his wife, and his two sons.
quoted.credit: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible (OSHB), morphology and lemmas by the OSHB project; text: Westminster Leningrad Codex (WLC)

examples.analysis: Walk through the verse in order. וַיְהִי is a wayyiqtol, 'and it happened'. בִּימֵי is a plural construct with the preposition ב, 'in the days of', and it runs into שְׁפֹט, an infinitive construct, 'the judging of'; הַשֹּׁפְטִים is a participle with the article, the subject of that judging. A second וַיְהִי brings in the famine: רָעָב is the subject and בָּאָרֶץ, 'in the land', the place. The verb וַיֵּלֶךְ is a wayyiqtol and its subject is אִישׁ, 'a man'. מִבֵּית לֶחֶם יְהוּדָה tells where he came from. לָגוּר is an infinitive with ל and shows his purpose, to sojourn; בִּשְׂדֵי מוֹאָב is another construct phrase with a preposition, 'in the fields of Moab'. The verse ends with the people who went with him: הוּא, וְאִשְׁתּוֹ with the suffix 'his', and וּשְׁנֵי בָנָיו, 'and his two sons', where שְׁנֵי is a construct dual and the suffix is again 'his'.

quoted.title: Ruth
quoted.english: Then she arose with her daughters-in-law, that she might return from the field of Moab; for she had heard in the field of Moab how that the LORD had remembered His people in giving them bread.
quoted.credit: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible (OSHB), morphology and lemmas by the OSHB project; text: Westminster Leningrad Codex (WLC)

examples.analysis: Two wayyiqtols, וַתָּקָם and וַתָּשָׁב, carry the action: 'she arose … and returned'. הִיא is the subject pronoun and וְכַלֹּתֶיהָ, 'and her daughters-in-law', is a noun with the suffix 'her', joined to it. מִשְּׂדֵי מוֹאָב is a construct phrase with מִן, 'from the fields of Moab'. Then two כִּי clauses with a qatal each: the first, כִּי שָׁמְעָה, gives the reason; the second, כִּי פָקַד יְהוָה אֶת עַמּוֹ, says what she heard. The suffix on עַמּוֹ is 'his'. The infinitive לָתֵת, 'to give', with לָהֶם and לָחֶם, tells what the Lord has done: he has visited his people to give them bread.

quoted.title: Ruth
quoted.english: And Ruth said: 'Entreat me not to leave thee, and to return from following after thee; for whither thou goest, I will go; and where thou lodgest, I will lodge; thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God;
quoted.credit: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible (OSHB), morphology and lemmas by the OSHB project; text: Westminster Leningrad Codex (WLC)

examples.analysis: Ruth's answer. וַתֹּאמֶר, a wayyiqtol, and then רוּת, the subject, open the speech. אַל with תִּפְגְּעִי, a jussive, is a prohibition: 'do not press me'. לְעָזְבֵךְ and לָשׁוּב are infinitives with ל, 'to leave you', 'to turn back'; the suffix of the first is 'you' (feminine). כִּי gives the reason. The next lines are pairs: אֶל אֲשֶׁר תֵּלְכִי אֵלֵךְ is 'to where you go I shall go', with no antecedent; וּבַאֲשֶׁר תָּלִינִי אָלִין is 'and where you lodge I shall lodge'. All four verbs are yiqtol. The last two clauses have no verb: עַמֵּךְ עַמִּי, 'your people (are) my people', and וֵאלֹהַיִךְ אֱלֹהָי, 'and your God (is) my God'. Each noun carries a suffix, 'your' or 'my', and the plural-form אֱלֹהִים is read as a singular here.

segments.credit: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible (OSHB), morphology and lemmas by the OSHB project; text: Westminster Leningrad Codex (WLC)

segments.title: Ruth
segments.english: The LORD grant you that ye may find rest, each of you in the house of her husband.' Then she kissed them; and they lifted up their voice, and wept.
segments.credit: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible (OSHB), morphology and lemmas by the OSHB project; text: Westminster Leningrad Codex (WLC)

segments.title: Ruth
segments.english: And they said unto her: 'Nay, but we will return with thee unto thy people.'
segments.credit: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible (OSHB), morphology and lemmas by the OSHB project; text: Westminster Leningrad Codex (WLC)

segments.title: Ruth
segments.english: And Naomi said: 'Turn back, my daughters; why will ye go with me? have I yet sons in my womb, that they may be your husbands?
segments.credit: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible (OSHB), morphology and lemmas by the OSHB project; text: Westminster Leningrad Codex (WLC)

segments.title: Ruth
segments.english: Turn back, my daughters, go your way; for I am too old to have a husband. If I should say: I have hope, should I even have an husband to-night, and also bear sons;
segments.credit: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible (OSHB), morphology and lemmas by the OSHB project; text: Westminster Leningrad Codex (WLC)

segments.title: Ruth
segments.english: would ye tarry for them till they were grown? would ye shut yourselves off for them and have no husbands? nay, my daughters; for it grieveth me much for your sakes, for the hand of the LORD is gone forth against me.'
segments.credit: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible (OSHB), morphology and lemmas by the OSHB project; text: Westminster Leningrad Codex (WLC)

segments.title: Ruth
segments.english: And they lifted up their voice, and wept again; and Orpah kissed her mother-in-law; but Ruth cleaved unto her.
segments.credit: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible (OSHB), morphology and lemmas by the OSHB project; text: Westminster Leningrad Codex (WLC)

segments.title: Ruth
segments.english: And she said: 'Behold, thy sister-in-law is gone back unto her people, and unto her god; return thou after thy sister-in-law.'
segments.credit: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible (OSHB), morphology and lemmas by the OSHB project; text: Westminster Leningrad Codex (WLC)
